moments.said: if I will use the LINE talk
moments.better: if I use LINE to talk
moments.why: After 'if', use the simple present for a possible future situation, not 'will'. Also, 'to talk' is more natural than 'the LINE talk'.
The third person singular subject 'my mom' needs the verb ending -s in the present simple.
The saving already happened, so use the past tense 'saved'.
A plural amount of money needs the plural 'dollars'.
'Underwear' is uncountable, so we count it with 'pairs of'.
Use '-ed' for how a person feels ('excited') and '-ing' for what causes the feeling ('exciting').

moments.said: I need a clean the clothes
moments.better: I need to clean the clothes
moments.why: After 'need', use 'to' plus the base verb: 'need to clean'.
'Clothes' is plural, so it takes 'are'.

moments.better: I need to check a bill
moments.why: 'Need' is followed by 'to' plus the base verb.
Country names usually don't take 'the'.

moments.said: I need listen to my coach
moments.better: I need to listen to my coach
moments.why: After 'need' use 'to' plus the base verb.
After a modal verb like 'can', use the base verb without -ing.

moments.said: you need speak English for everybody
moments.better: you need to speak English to everybody
moments.why: Use 'need to' plus the base verb, and 'speak to' someone.

moments.said: I scared talking with the, the other people
moments.better: I'm scared of talking with the other people
moments.why: 'Scared' needs the verb 'be' ('I'm') and the preposition 'of' before -ing.

moments.said: the coach need say you need to go
moments.better: the coach needs to say you need to go
moments.why: Use 'needs' with a singular subject, followed by 'to' and the base verb.
Do not use the comparative 'cheaper' after 'very'; use the plain adjective 'cheap'.
Use the past tense for a past trip, and country names usually have no 'the'.

moments.said: the Italy have a many, many, uh, liar
moments.why: Country names have no 'the', 'Italy' takes 'has', and 'many' goes with a plural noun without 'a'.
'Money' is uncountable, so use 'some' and not 'a'.

moments.said: you have a finish a big project
moments.better: you have finished a big project
moments.why: The present perfect is 'have' plus the past participle 'finished'.

moments.said: many, many company is a small company
moments.better: many, many companies are small companies
moments.why: 'Many' needs a plural noun and a plural verb.
In English the usual pattern is 'it's rainy all day', with 'all day' at the end.
'Cold' is an adjective here, so it does not take 'a'.
'Near' is not usually placed before a noun like this. 'Nearby' goes after it.

moments.said: have a many, many fish boat
moments.why: The singular subject '旗津' takes 'has'. 'Many' needs no 'a' and a plural noun, and 'fishing boats' is the natural phrase.

moments.said: Maybe you can go to the sunset.
moments.better: Maybe you can go see the sunset.
moments.why: You 'go see' or 'watch' a sunset. 'Go to' is for places.
Use the plural 'months' after 'two'.
'T-shirt' is a countable noun, so it needs 'a' or a plural form.
Use 'lower than' to compare temperatures. 'Down than' is not a standard comparison.

moments.better: has been raining there for a long time
moments.why: An action that started in the past and continues now uses the present perfect continuous, and 'for a long time' needs 'for a'.
Grandma is a woman, so the pronoun should be 'she'.

patterns.title: Missing 'to' after 'need'
patterns.tip: After 'need', use 'to' plus the base verb: 'I need to check', 'you need to speak'. With he/she/it, add -s to 'need': 'the coach needs to say'.

patterns.title: Subject-verb agreement
patterns.tip: Make the verb match the subject. Singular subjects take -s ('my mom says', 'Italy has'). Plural subjects like 'clothes' and 'many companies' take 'are'.

patterns.title: Adding 'the' before country names
patterns.tip: Most country names don't take 'the': say 'I go to Germany' and 'I went to Italy'.

patterns.title: Extra 'a' before uncountable nouns, 'many' and adjectives
patterns.tip: Don't use 'a' before 'many', before uncountable nouns like 'money', or before a bare adjective like 'cold'. Use 'some money', 'many fishing boats' and 'It's cold'.

patterns.title: Plural endings and missing articles on countable nouns
patterns.tip: Add -s to countable nouns after a number ('two months', '2,000 dollars'). Singular countable nouns need 'a', as in 'a T-shirt'. Uncountable nouns like 'underwear' need a measure phrase, as in 'two pairs of underwear'.

patterns.title: Past tense and perfect forms
patterns.tip: Use the past tense for finished events ('saved', 'went'). Use have + past participle for the present perfect ('have finished'), and 'has been raining for a long time' for something still continuing.
